run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-15T08:19:25Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The frontend RequestErrorRate alert (namespace otel-demo, severity warning, per the delivered alert payload first firing at 2026-11-15T08:19:25Z) is explained by a datastore failure one hop below frontend on the cart path. Frontend's own error spans were zero through 07:48:25 and then rose to a peak of about 1.88 spans/s at 07:56:25; every frontend operation carrying errors is a cart or checkout operation (POST /api/cart, executing api route (pages) /api/cart, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart, POST /api/checkout, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder). The deepest cause the evidence supports is pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft: its valkey-cart container was last terminated with reason OOMKilled and exitCode 137 (started 08:22:13Z, finished 08:22:24Z), it has restartCount 4 and is now in CrashLoopBackOff with ready=false, and the valkey-cart Service endpoint set contains only notReadyAddresses. The valkey-cart Deployment limits memory to 10Mi with a 4Mi request, far below sibling workloads (cart 165Mi, checkout 512Mi). The cart pod confirms the effect in its own logs: repeated "Wasn't able to connect to redis" with error statuses raised, while cart's VALKEY_ADDR is correctly valkey-cart:6379. Checkout's error spans are its client calls to CartService/GetCart and EmptyCart plus its PlaceOrder server span, i.e. the same cart dependency, and frontend-proxy records its own error spans on 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress'. Chain supported by evidence: valkey-cart OOM and crash-loop, no ready endpoint, cart cannot reach its datastore and errors, frontend and checkout error on cart/checkout routes, alert fires. The exact alert expression and its reported value 3.0222 could not be reproduced from metrics (no alert rules returned), and the retained working-set samples for the valkey-cart container stayed around 3.5-3.9MiB, so the specific allocation that hit the 10Mi limit is not visible.

claims.text: For service_name=frontend, traces_span_metrics_calls_total{status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"} was 0 at every step up to 07:48:25 and then rose: 0.0296 at 07:49:25, 0.1778 at 07:51:25, 1.348 at 07:52:25, peaking at 1.8791666666666667 spans/s at 07:56:25, then 1.488 at 07:58:25, 1.258 at 07:59:25 and 1.025 at 08:00:25; in the same result frontend STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans moved from about 12.5/s to about 45/s, so total frontend span volume was also higher.

The frontend error spans are concentrated on cart and checkout operations: executing api route (pages) /api/cart reached 0.5/s, POST /api/cart 0.3708/s, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem 0.2542/s, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 0.2458/s, POST /api/checkout and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and executing api route (pages) /api/checkout each 0.0708/s, all first non-zero around 07:49-07:52 and still non-zero at the last returned point 08:00:25; frontend's GET /api/data, executing api route (pages) /api/data, grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds and tcp.connect had zero error spans throughout.

The cart service itself records error spans on its own server operations: POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem reached 0.2583/s, POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 0.2667/s and POST /oteldemo.CartService/EmptyCart 0.00425/s, all first non-zero at 07:49:25.

In the service-by-service error-span query, cart (peak 0.5293/s at 07:56:25), frontend (peak 1.879/s), frontend-proxy (peak 1.354/s) and checkout (peak 0.1768/s) are the services with materially elevated error spans; payment and accounting are 0 at every returned point and ad, fraud-detection and recommendation stay at or below 0.0047/s across the window.

checkout's error spans are on the cart dependency and its own entry point: oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 0.0493/s, oteldemo.CartService/EmptyCart 0.00411/s, oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 0.0863/s and HTTP POST 0.037/s.
frontend-proxy records its own error spans on span_name 'ingress' (up to 1.0556/s at 07:54:25) and 'router frontend egress' (up to 0.1407/s) in the same period.

The cart pod cart-755465879b-4p8d9 logs repeatedly show "Wasn't able to connect to redis" immediately followed by "Error status code ... with detail ... raised" between 08:25:59Z and 08:26:48Z; 324 lines in the retained stream matched the redis/error filter.
The cart Deployment sets VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379 and the valkey-cart Service exists on port 6379 with selector opentelemetry.io/name=valkey-cart, so the cart client address is not misconfigured.

Pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft has phase Running but ready=false: container valkey-cart lastState.terminated.reason=OOMKilled with exitCode=137, startedAt 2026-11-15T08:22:13Z and finishedAt 2026-11-15T08:22:24Z; restartCount=4, started=false, state.waiting.reason=CrashLoopBackOff with message 'back-off 1m20s restarting failed container', and Ready/ContainersReady=False (ContainersNotReady) since 08:22:24Z on a pod started 07:41:45Z.

The valkey-cart Deployment specifies container valkey-cart resources limits {cpu 10m, memory 10Mi} and requests {cpu 2m, memory 4Mi}, and reports unavailableReplicas=1 with Available=False (MinimumReplicasUnavailable) since 2026-11-15T08:22:24Z; in the same query the cart Deployment limits are {cpu 45m, memory 165Mi} and checkout {cpu 250m, memory 512Mi}.

The valkey-cart Service endpoints object contains only notReadyAddresses (100.96.5.138, targetRef Pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft) and no ready addresses, while the cart and checkout endpoints each contain one ready address.

Events on the valkey-cart pod in the window show container valkey-cart Pulled and Created at 08:23:57Z, Started at 08:23:59Z (count 6) and a Warning BackOff 'Back-off restarting failed container' at 08:26:41Z with count 22.

Every other otel-demo pod (accounting, ad, cart, checkout, currency, email, flagd, fraud-detection, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, kafka, load-generator, otel-collector, payment, postgresql, product-catalog, quote, recommendation, shipping) is Running with ready=true and restartCount 0, started 07:41:45Z-07:48Z; valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft is the only pod with ready=false and it carries restartCount 4 with last termination reason OOMKilled.

Deepest supported cause: the valkey-cart container is being killed by its container memory limit (10Mi), which is far too small for a valkey server, so it restarts into CrashLoopBackOff; with the valkey-cart Service having no ready endpoint, cart's redis client fails ("Wasn't able to connect to redis"), cart returns errors on AddItem/GetCart, and frontend and checkout error on cart and checkout routes, producing the frontend RequestErrorRate alert. Supporting evidence: kubelet-reported OOMKilled with exit 137 eleven seconds after container start, restartCount 4, BackOff events with count 22, a Service with only notReady addresses, and a 10Mi limit against 165Mi/512Mi on the sibling cart and checkout workloads.

A traffic ramp may have contributed to reaching the valkey memory ceiling: frontend STATUS_CODE_UNSET span rate rose from about 12.5/s at 07:24:25 to about 45/s by 07:33:25, before the cart and frontend error onset, and frontend/checkout traffic is what drives cart's redis reads and writes (AddItem/GetCart). This is a time coincidence in the data, not a demonstrated causal link.

container_memory_working_set_bytes for container valkey-cart in pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft was only about 3.5-3.9MiB in every recorded sample (3538944, 3919872, 3829760 bytes and similar), never approaching a 10Mi (10485760 byte) limit, so the retained samples do not themselves show the memory spike that triggered the OOMKill and the exact allocation that exceeded the limit is unknown.

frontend kept serving most sampled requests successfully: the 60 longest frontend spans in the slice spanning 07:58:23-07:58:26 all have status_state recorded with http.status_code 200 or rpc.grpc.status_code 0, including POST /api/cart, GET /api/cart, POST /api/checkout and grpc calls to CartService, CheckoutService and ProductCatalogService, so the failures are a minority of frontend traffic rather than a total outage.

Cart-side redis/valkey address misconfiguration as the cause was rejected: cart's VALKEY_ADDR is valkey-cart:6379, the valkey-cart Service exists on port 6379 with the matching selector opentelemetry.io/name=valkey-cart, and the cart logs fail with "Wasn't able to connect to redis" while the valkey-cart pod is not ready and its Service has no ready endpoint.

The cart application itself crashing or being resource-killed was rejected: cart-755465879b-4p8d9 is Running and ready with restartCount 0 and no last termination reason, the cart Deployment reports readyReplicas 1 with Available=True, and its logged errors are redis connection failures rather than its own OOM or restart.

Raise the valkey-cart container memory limit and request in Deployment valkey-cart to a realistic valkey footprint instead of the current limits {cpu 10m, memory 10Mi} and requests {memory 4Mi}, for example several hundred MiB, so the datastore stops being OOMKilled; then confirm pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft becomes Ready, the valkey-cart endpoint moves from notReadyAddresses into ready addresses, and the cart "Wasn't able to connect to redis" log lines and frontend/checkout cart-route error spans stop.

gaps: The alert's own rule definition and the origin of its reported 'current: 3.0222' value could not be verified from telemetry: list_prometheus_rules returned no_data for rule_name RequestErrorRate (b9168f0d-3d4a-4054-9016-2b8539daaf9b-t0:27361547-2286-460e-8981-c0a5e1f0e76c) and for all alerting rules (75627ff6-80ab-4b1a-9f43-39bd3cb0c0a9-t1:3af23bab-ede5-4855-a153-ce4e45edc3fb), and get_all_labels for http_server_request_duration_seconds_count returned no_data (358806a4-606a-4025-9830-93ab355e57c1-t0:c36620cd-3af6-4b8c-b710-ea6b18d55360); the alert labels and timestamps are taken from the delivered alert payload only.

Change history integration is not available in this Run (listed as not_integrated), so I cannot determine whether the valkey-cart 10Mi memory limit and 4Mi request were recently introduced, who changed them, or what the prior values were; the container image valkey/valkey:8.1.3-alpine is unchanged across the observed restarts.

The retained container_memory_working_set_bytes samples for the valkey-cart container (about 3.5-3.9MiB) never approach the 10Mi limit, so the moment of memory exhaustion is not observable; a namespace LimitRange cannot be checked because that kind is not supported in this Run, and node-level memory pressure was not examined.

Trace data is a very narrow sample: the frontend trace search covered only 07:58:23-07:58:26 for the whole 07:19-08:38 window, and tag searches error=true on cart (6198492e-9169-4b46-baf3-17f80b903fac-t0:137c9f79-cd22-483d-894a-a7e369565529) and http.status_code="500" on frontend (5756b312-ace5-4289-8061-840e672963a1-t0:7acfcadf-eb7a-42d8-bb89-b2c51a46ee0e) returned no traces, so no individual failing trace or its error detail could be cited; span counts are not request counts.

The valkey-cart container produced no readable log lines: the current stream was empty and no previous instance existed (78543344-9222-4833-b507-9181594ea90b-t0:9d76d8d7-955a-4239-9576-af81a42155d8), and the frontend pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-x9gbm returned no log lines in the retained window (42120f58-29b9-4cf6-9104-2b7da9bb4f56-t0:7669f290-9485-4c83-aaf6-db4c32fb43e1); application-log confirmation therefore exists only for the cart pod.

Frontend error series returned points only up to about 08:00-08:02 while the alert started 08:19:25, so frontend error-rate behaviour between 08:02 and 08:38 is unknown from metrics; continuity of the failure into the alert time rests on cart logs at 08:25-08:26 and on pod, Deployment and endpoint state observed at 08:38.

Services currency, email, image-provider, kafka, product-catalog, quote and shipping have no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series in the query result, which is unknown rather than zero; no ingress or NetworkPolicy object review succeeded (NetworkPolicy and LimitRange queries returned no_data or unsupported, e35abf71-f8db-4eb1-98ea-93ca07a25c4a-t0:9191c1ae-e9a2-4238-b691-de9a09889c2b).

The pod-level memory limit query for valkey-cart returned no_data (7749f3e9-edf8-433c-8a18-7778a8e15a4e-t0:ae987e91-283c-4cf4-a28c-087f0a0dd630), so the 10Mi limit is taken from the Deployment manifest and pod spec rather than from a metric series.
next_steps: Have a cluster owner review the valkey-cart Deployment resource limits and requests and any LimitRange in otel-demo, and check change history for when memory was set to 10Mi.
After raising the valkey-cart memory limit, verify the Deployment's unavailableReplicas returns to 0 and the valkey-cart Service endpoints contain ready addresses.
Confirm whether the load-generator traffic ramp is intentional and whether cart's redis working set scales with it, to size the valkey-cart memory limit.
Obtain the alerting rule definition from the Prometheus/Alertmanager configuration owner to confirm which metric expression produces the 3.0222 request-error-rate value.
